passage:
The town library gave children a stamp card for summer reading. For every book they finished, they received one stamp. Ten stamps could be exchanged for a small notebook.
Some children chose only short books to get stamps quickly. Others chose longer books they truly liked.
At the end of summer, the librarian asked children to share their favorite book. Some with many stamps could not remember their stories well. A girl with only four stamps described one book in detail and made everyone want to read it.
The librarian smiled. "Stamps are fun," she said, "but the real prize is what stays in your mind."
The stamp card brought children to books. The books had to do the rest.
